Title: Personal experience drives Fadhlina's push for better caregiver support for working mothers
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said her personal experiences of child abuse and loss had strengthened her commitment to improving caregiver support for working mothers.
Fadhlina said her second child was abused by a caregiver who hit the child on the legs while she was working as a lawyer with a demanding schedule.
"I felt very guilty because, as a working mother and a lawyer at that time, my work schedule was very tight.
"I had no choice but to send my child to a caregiver," she said in her speech at Himpunan Gala Pesona Kasih Madani here today.
She said the experience convinced her that caregivers must demonstrate greater commitment, have access to training opportunities and understand their responsibility towards the community.
Fadhlina, who has six children, said three of them had been placed under the care of caregivers, adding that finding suitable childcare was a major challenge for working mothers.
Her experience was compounded by the death of her fourth child from Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), which she said left her traumatised and forced her to confront the difficult choice of whether to continue working or care for her children herself.
"I had to think about whether to continue working or stop and take care of my children," she said.
Fadhlina said support from her extended family, particularly her siblings, had helped her cope while continuing to work.
She said the experience underscored the importance of building a wider childcare ecosystem that would give working mothers confidence that their children were safe and properly cared for.
"This is how caregivers support working mothers like us, who are constantly thinking about our children's safety while we work," she added.
Fadhlina also backed efforts to expand the Kasih Madani caregiver programme, saying trained and accredited caregivers could help strengthen child protection at the community level.
She said she had conveyed the importance of the programme to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and would seek its inclusion in next year's Budget to enable more women to receive support.
Fadhlina said child protection should extend beyond childcare centres to schools, with everyone in the community sharing responsibility for safeguarding children.
"It takes a village to raise a child," she said, stressing that caregivers, schools, policymakers, parents and community organisations all had a role to play in protecting
children.
She said expanding the number of trained caregivers would also contribute to women's empowerment by allowing mothers to work with greater peace of mind.
More than 230 home-based caregivers from Penang and Kedah were recognised today at Himpunan Gala Pesona Kasih Madani, marking their progress through training and professional development aimed at strengthening the quality of early childcare in their communities.
Since its launch in August last year, Kasih Madani has reached more than 1,000 caregivers across four states: Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah and Penang.
Managed by Merdeka Centre with the support of the Finance Ministry through Yayasan Sime Darby, Kasih Madani is a government-driven initiative aimed at strengthening Malaysia's childcare ecosystem by empowering and building the capacity of home-based and community caregivers.
Through programmes such as Kursus Rintis Asuhan Madani and Seminar Asuhan Madani, caregivers are equipped with the knowledge and skills to improve the quality and safety of the childcare they provide.
Around 200 participants have been selected for the Bimbingan Keterampilan Profesionalisasi Asuhan Madani Professionalisation Programme, which provides a pathway for caregivers to further develop their capabilities and professional standing.

Title: 27 illegal snares destroyed in Selangor, Perak wildlife operation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 27 illegal snares were destroyed during the Integrated Khazanah Operation (OBK) at several wildlife crime hotspots in forests in Selangor and Perak recently.
The enforcement patrols were conducted from Aug 11 to 25 by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan), General Operations Force (GOP), Marine Police Force (PPM), Perak State Parks Corporation and Selangor Forestry Department.
Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the 27 snares comprised spring traps, wire loop snares and nylon loop snares.
"The figure does not include other traps and devices that were also found during the patrols.
"The type and size of snares used generally depend on the species of wildlife being targeted.
"Spring traps are commonly used to target wild boar, while wire and nylon loop snares can be used to target larger or smaller wildlife, depending on the diameter of the wire or rope and the size of the spring mechanism used," he said in a statement today.
He said, in theory, the larger the snare and spring mechanism used, the larger the wildlife that could potentially be caught.
He said that in some cases, snares might be set to target specific species such as tigers, but could also trap other wildlife passing through the area.
"Moreover, snares are often concealed and camouflaged with their surroundings to reduce the chances of detection.
"This puts non-target species at risk of serious injury or death if they become trapped and are not freed within a short period," he said.
Abdul Kadir said cooperation between agencies through continuous patrols and targeted enforcement was among the key preventive measures to protect wildlife and their habitats from encroachment by irresponsible individuals.
He said illegal snaring not only threatened wildlife species but also affected the flora and fauna that formed part of the country's natural heritage.

Title: 11 detained to assist probe into group attack in Ipoh
Article:
IPOH: Police have detained 11 individuals to assist in investigations into a group attack that left a victim seriously injured in Taman Pengkalan Jaya here on Tuesday (Sept 1).
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 26-year-old victim was approached by five men travelling in two cars at about 10.30am, who then chased and assaulted him.
He said the victim, in an attempt to escape, jumped into Sungai Kinta but was slashed with a machete by one of the suspects, sustaining injuries to his face, hands, legs and back.
Mohd Alwi said members of the public later came to the victim's aid before taking him to hospital for treatment.
"The incident was believed to have been motivated by revenge and dissatisfaction by an organised crime group against the victim," he said in a statement last night.
Mohd Alwi said all those arrested, aged between 22 and 41, had previous criminal records involving drug offences and violent crimes.
He said they had been remanded to assist in investigations under Section 326 of the Penal Code.
Mohd Alwi also urged anyone with information on illegal activities involving organised crime groups to report it through the police operations room's official channels or at the nearest police station.
–BERNAMA

Title: From janitor to senior lecturer: UM academic turns experience into PhD research
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: From collecting rubbish as a janitor to becoming a senior lecturer at Universiti Malaya, Dr Nurul Asmaa Akmal Md Din has turned years of hard work into an academic career.
Nurul Asmaa, 30, drew on her experience in waste management for her doctoral research.
She began working as a janitor in 2018 after completing her studies, initially taking the job because she needed an income, according to Harian Metro.
"I worked as a janitor because I needed a job that could earn me money immediately.
"I was paid daily," she said.
She said the job proved valuable rather than a setback, with her experience in waste management later forming the basis of her PhD research.
"My PhD research was on waste management, which required me to draw on my experience working in the sector and collecting data for the study," she said.
Nurul Asmaa later pursued her ambition of becoming a lecturer and is now a senior lecturer at UM.
She said her journey was driven by a belief that hard work would eventually bear fruit.
"Hard work will never betray the results.
"No matter how difficult what we are working towards may be, all the exhaustion will eventually pay off," she said.
Nurul Asmaa also credited her mother for encouraging her to pursue her studies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas-Umno ummah unity must move beyond resolutions, says Tuan Ibrahim
Article:
KOTA BARU: The ummah unity between Pas and Umno, which was unanimously endorsed at the Islamist party's muktamar, must be translated into action.
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said support for the unity would usually be tested when negotiations on seat allocations for the general election begin.
He said that at that point, any decisions reached must be upheld based on the principles of wala' and thiqah, namely loyalty to and trust in the party's decisions.
"The muktamar has unanimously approved the strengthening of ummah unity, particularly with many people talking about unity or cooperation between Pas and Umno.
"I want to remind everyone that our unanimous decision to support this will be tested by Allah after this, and usually seat negotiations will become an issue whenever there is political cooperation.
"At that point, all of us will be required to ensure that the decision we make today is upheld based on wala' and thiqah. We must understand that a grand vision needs to be completed.
"It is not merely about achieving unity in the context of unanimously approving the motion, but it must be translated into compliance with what the party has decided," he said.
He said this in his winding-up speech at the 72nd Pas Muktamar here today.
Tuan Ibrahim said the Muslim Unity Committee and Seat Negotiation Committee were among the important matters that needed attention as part of the agenda or action plan following the approval of the resolution.
Therefore, he said, the ummah unity resolution should be driven by a committee that would serve as an agent for the agenda and decisions.
"Similarly, in the context of elections, the Seat Negotiation Committee is a body appointed and decided upon by the party to look at the overall picture, not just the seats we have won.
"We will uphold the principle that seats won will remain with the party that won them, and Pas will defend the seats we have won," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze-linked health problems on the rise, asthma cases jump eightfold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asthma, bronchitis, acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis are among the health problems reported to have increased amid the haze currently blanketing the country.
Public health medicine specialist Datuk Dr Zainal Ariffin Omar said the increase was linked to inflammation of the respiratory tract caused by haze.
"Recent developments show that asthma cases have increased more than eightfold.
"URTI occurs when haze pollutants weaken the lungs' defences, making it easier for viruses and bacteria to attack.
"Conjunctivitis can also occur as haze particles directly irritate the eyes," he said.
The Health Ministry (MOH), in a statement last week, said asthma cases had increased to 1,811.
Dr Zainal said fine particles in haze could irritate the respiratory tract, making the body more susceptible to viral and bacterial infections.
"Studies have found that air pollution increases the incidence of respiratory tract infections.
"The main concerns are severe breathing difficulties and lung infections such as pneumonia," he said.
He said this could lead to increased hospital admissions, particularly among children under 5 and the elderly.
Dr Zainal said children and the elderly were among those most vulnerable to the effects of haze because their immune systems and lung functions were weaker.
"People with chronic conditions such as asthma, heart disease and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are also at risk of developing health complications from exposure to haze.
"Pregnant women and smokers should also take precautions as they face higher health risks when exposed to air pollution," he said.

Title: Transform old assets to create new economic value, says Johari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Old assets that are no longer being utilised optimally should be transformed to create new economic value, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said.
The Investment, Trade and Industry Minister said investors' willingness to take risks, backed by capital, creativity and sound management, could revitalise old assets while benefiting the surrounding business ecosystem.
"Assets that are no longer in use do not necessarily lose their value simply because they are old or no longer being utilised optimally.
"I would like to specifically commend Menara Rezeki and UDA for having the courage to recognise the potential of an old building and give it a new lease of life.
"This is the kind of courage we want to see in entrepreneurship and investment. In entrepreneurship and investment, we cannot avoid taking risks," he said when launching Chinatown 1974 at Petaling Street here today.
Johari, who is also the Titiwangsa Member of Parliament, said Chinatown 1974 symbolised the entrepreneurial spirit of identifying opportunities where others might not see them and taking the bold step of turning those opportunities into reality.
"Equipped with vision, capital, creativity and sound management, such assets can be given a second life and, in turn, create new economic value," he said.
Chinatown 1974 is a new eight-storey landmark at Petaling Street that showcases a retro Nanyang heritage lifestyle inspired by the 1970s.
Its facilities include a traditional kopitiam, a dim sum restaurant and halal steamboat options, offering visitors a diverse culinary experience. The building also houses The Seven Stars Hotel.
Another attraction is the rooftop bar, which offers views of the surrounding area, including Kuala Lumpur's iconic Merdeka 118 landmark.
Meanwhile, Johari said Chinatown 1974 was not merely the redevelopment of an old building, but also had the potential to create employment opportunities, attract tourists and benefit local entrepreneurs and suppliers.
"We want to see greater economic returns from this area, local businesses grow and existing assets put to the best possible use.
"We have many old areas with their own stories, heritage and identity. The question is how we can revive these areas without taking away their original character and identity.
"For me, Chinatown 1974 provides a good example. If we can give a second life to a building, we may also be able to give a new lease of life to an entire area and community," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Human-wildlife conflict complaints hit 76,000, losses top RM58.7mil
Article:
KUALA BERANG: Complaints over human-wildlife conflicts nationwide, particularly those involving elephants, have reached 76,000 since 2021, with property and crop damage exceeding RM58.7 million.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the rising number of complaints was a cause for concern.
He said the increase in conflicts was largely due to large-scale land clearing for agriculture and development, which destroyed and encroached on elephants' traditional roaming areas.
"Besides the increasingly serious threat posed by elephants, complaints received by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) also involve other species, such as monkeys and tigers," he said.
He said this after officiating the handover ceremony for the Malaysia Madani Adopted Village and Adopted School project at Kampung Basong here today.
Also present was Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim.
Arthur said a comprehensive solution involving short-, medium- and long-term action plans must be implemented immediately to ensure the balance of the ecosystem while allowing for the state's development.
He said the government would continue to prioritise public safety, even though it costs RM68,000 to relocate elephants to their natural habitat.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Enough fighting,' Sanusi tells off 'stubborn' Perlis PN leaders
Article:
KOTA BARU: Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Noor has reminded Perlis Perikatan Nasional  leaders to stop bickering and avoid repeating the conflicts that have previously plagued the coalition in the state.
Sanusi, who is also Pas election director, said the same reminder had been issued before, but the infighting had instead become worse.
"I told the people of Perlis not to fight, but they kept fighting and it got even worse... that's enough.
"You people are stubborn. What people told you not to do, you did.  Now, no one is going to treat you anymore, so treat yourselves.
"Insya-Allah, there will be no more fighting after this," he said whEH winding up the debate on the Pas president's policy speech at the 72nd Pas Muktamar here today.
It was previously reported that the Perlis Pas Youth wing had urged the Pas and PN leadership to consider stern action against Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah, who was alleged to be increasingly tarnishing the image of PN and Pas in the state
.
Its delegate, Ali Na'imi Ahmad Azizi, was reported to have said the matter should be taken seriously as Perlis is governed by a PN administration with Pas, yet Pas assemblymen were allegedly being treated like opposition representatives.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man arrested with RM1.46mil worth of vape pods in Tumpat
Article:
TUMPAT: A man was arrested after being found in possession of more than 14,600 vape pods worth RM1.46 million in an operation at Kampung Kutan, Pasir Pekan, here, last night.
General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the seizure was made at about 7.40pm under Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan.
He said, acting on public tip-offs, a team stopped the 22-year-old suspect in front of a mosque in Pengkalan Kubor.
"An initial body search found no illegal items. However, during questioning, the suspect admitted to keeping contraband.
"About 11.30pm, the suspect led the team to a house in Kampung Kutan, Pasir Pekan, where officers found 14,600 vape pods of various flavours in the living room.
"The suspect admitted to being involved in smuggling vape pods for about two years and was paid RM50 for each box he handled.
"The vape pods were then smuggled into Thailand through an illegal jetty in Pengkalan Kubor," he said.
Radzi said the vape pods were believed to be smuggled from Malaysia to Thailand due to high demand there.
"Vapes and electronic cigarettes remain prohibited in Thailand, including their possession, use, import, export and sale," he said.
The suspect, from Kampung Kok Pauh in Pengkalan Kubor, also has a previous record under Section 8 of the Betting Act 1953, he added.
The suspect and seized items were handed over to the Tumpat District Health Office for further action.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 3(1) of the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Govt ready to declare emergency if API exceeds 400
Article:
KUALA BERANG: The government is prepared to propose a state of emergency in areas recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of above 400, in line with national haze management standard operating procedures.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said three areas, which are Kuching, Kota Samarahan, and Sri Aman have recorded very unhealthy air quality levels.
He said the government will focus cloud seeding operations on these three areas where the API exceeds 400.
"Out of 68 air pollution monitoring stations, only three recorded very unhealthy air levels.
"The three stations recording very unhealthy readings are in Kuching, Kota Samarahan, and Sri Aman, while one station in Serian continues to record hazardous readings," he told reporters here today.
On the API level in Serian, where an emergency was declared, Arthur said the government will continue cloud seeding operations to reduce haze levels.
He said cloud seeding operations in several parts of Sarawak and northern Peninsular Malaysia, including Kedah and Perlis, produced positive results, with rain starting yesterday afternoon and continuing until early this morning.
"The government has received written approval from the Indonesian government allowing aerial assets to enter the republic's airspace for cloud seeding operations.
"We have conducted cloud seeding operations in Sarawak and are prepared to expand operations using aerial assets across the border," he said.
Commenting on Malaysian plantation companies allegedly conducting open burning, Arthur said the Indonesian government will take appropriate action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas will not surrender potential winning seats, says Sanusi
Article:
KOTA BHARU: Pas will not surrender seats identified as potential wins to any party for the 16th General Election (GE16).
Pas central election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said these winnable seats will be identified by the party's central and state election machinery.
"We will determine which seats have winning potential. We must not give away those seats to anyone.
"Giving away seats we can win while taking seats where we are likely to lose is what people call being sincere and foolish," he said during his winding-up speech on the President's Policy Address at the 70th Pas Annual Muktamar here today.
At the same time, Sanusi reminded Pas leaders not to feel inferior when negotiating with other parties, adding that the party should not show humility to those who are not humble.
"Today, Pas is an elephant. When a cat with two or three kittens passes by, we become afraid.
"They just formed a party two days ago, then came to teach us, and we followed them. That is wrong," he said.
He also urged the party machinery to strengthen its workforce to face GE16, which is now less than 300 days away.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tok Mat : DNA samples of 55 Malaysians' next of kin ready for Nepal matching
Article:
SEREMBAN: DNA samples from the next of kin of 55 Malaysians previously reported as unreachable following devastating floods in Nepal have been obtained, completing the required sample collection.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the samples would be sent to Nepal soon for DNA matching.
"We have just completed collecting DNA samples from all the victims' immediate family members, and the samples will be sent to Nepal for matching. Since there are many victims, it will take some time to complete the process.
"If necessary, we may send experts from the Chemistry Department to assist the Nepalese authorities in identifying the victims and conducting DNA matching to expedite the process.
"Other countries have also indicated that they would send their respective DNA experts to help expedite the matching process," he told reporters after opening the Karnival Kemerdekaan Pinggiran Senawang 2026 at the Taman Pinggiran Senawang playground here today.
Yesterday, Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih) representative Dr R. Manivannan said 52 next of kin had completed their submissions, while the remaining three were scheduled to do so on Sept 4. (https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1525485/dna-samples-52-relatives-missing-malaysians-nepal-submitted)
Meanwhile, on the 11-member Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) which departed for Nepal today, Mohamad said the team was equipped with
various equipment
, including five high-capacity drones and communication devices.
"They will assist the Nepalese authorities in tracking down survivors, particularly in areas that are difficult to reach manually.
"The affected area stretches across a vast region from Tibet through Nepal towards India. The slopes and ravines are dangerous, so using drones is one way to facilitate and support search and rescue efforts," he said.
Mohamad said the Nepalese authorities had so far provided full cooperation to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu.
"I receive daily reports from our Chargé d'Affaires there on developments, and we thank the Nepalese authorities, especially my counterpart, Shisir Khanal.
"He has given permission for our Smart team to assist, as many Malaysians are involved," he said.
Mohamad said the government had been regularly updating the victims' family members on developments in Nepal through an operations room that had been established.
He said the government would not release information indiscriminately to the public, with updates only being provided to registered family members as a measure of respect for those involved.
"I believe the search and rescue operation will be suspended in the near future, and at present, the operation is focused solely on recovery efforts," he said.
Earlier, the media reported that 55 Malaysians remained unaccounted for following flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa district on Aug 26.
The Malaysians'
fate remained unknown
following severe floods and landslides that struck the district near the Nepal-China border.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Don't rush GE16 seat talks, says Johari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Discussions regarding seat allocations between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the 16th General Election (GE16) should be left to the top leaders of both coalitions, says Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
The Umno vice-president said that every political party naturally seeks to defend the seats it won in the previous election and seat allocations should not complicate efforts to build an understanding between BN and PN.
"Pas wants to defend its seats, and Umno also wants to defend the seats it won. All political parties are like that.
"But if they want to work together, let the two presidents discuss it. If I interfere, it will only make things complicated," he told reporters after officiating Chinatown 1974 at Petaling Street here today.
Johari said that it is still too early to make rushed decisions on seat negotiations, given that GE16 is still some time away.
"Don't complicate things…take it slow. The election is still a long way off," he said.
His comments follow statements made yesterday by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang during his presidential address at the 72nd Pas Muktamar in Kota Baru.
Hadi said that the party intends to defend all Parliamentary and State Assembly seats it won in GE15.
The Marang Member of Parliament said that Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah, and Perlis must be defended, strengthened administratively, and governed according to the Islamic agenda within state constitutional limits.
Hadi said that future electoral gains would come from Pahang, Perak, and Selangor, boosting the overall parliamentary presence of Pas and PN.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From completion to excellence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Successfully completing a project at the workplace is more than the achievement of a deadline or the delivery of an expected outcome.
It represents a collective moment of accomplishment in which effort, collaboration, perseverance and responsibility come together. When teams experience this success, something important often happens beyond the project itself: motivation grows, confidence strengthens and a desire for excellence begins to take root.
Every project presents challenges. Team members must navigate competing priorities, solve problems, communicate effectively and remain focused despite setbacks. When those efforts eventually produce a successful result, individuals can see tangible evidence that their contributions mattered. This sense of achievement can become a powerful source of motivation.
Success also creates confidence. A team that has successfully overcome a difficult challenge begins to believe that it can overcome the next one. This confidence is particularly important when people are faced with unfamiliar responsibilities or ambitious objectives. Previous success becomes evidence that challenges are manageable when everyone works together with purpose.
The completion of a project can also strengthen a team's sense of identity. People who have worked towards a common objective and achieved it develop a shared experience. They understand one another's strengths, recognise the value of collaboration and often develop greater trust. The next project therefore begins with a stronger foundation than the previous one.
Recognition plays an important role in this process. When leaders acknowledge the contribution of team members, employees are more likely to feel valued. Recognition does not necessarily have to involve financial rewards or formal awards. A sincere acknowledgement of someone's effort, creativity, reliability or leadership can have a significant effect on morale.
However, successful completion should not be treated as the end of the journey. The most effective organisations use achievement as an opportunity for reflection. Teams should ask what worked well, what could have been done differently and what lessons can be carried forward. This turns success into learning rather than simply celebration.
This process is fundamental to the pursuit of excellence. Excellence is rarely achieved through one extraordinary effort. It develops through continuous improvement, where people examine their performance and look for ways to become more effective. A completed project provides a valuable reference point from which that improvement can begin.
When your colleagues see that their ideas have contributed to success, they are also more likely to participate actively in future projects. They become willing to offer suggestions, challenge assumptions and take ownership of problems. A successful experience can therefore transform your team members from passive participants into engaged contributors.
Leadership has a particularly important responsibility in creating this environment. Leaders should celebrate achievement without creating complacency. The message should be that success is something to be proud of but also something from which the team can build. The question should not simply be, "Did we succeed?" but also, "How can we do even better next time?"
This distinction is crucial. If success becomes the only measure of performance, teams may become satisfied with achieving minimum expectations. Excellence requires a different mindset. It encourages people to ask whether a process can be improved, whether communication can be clearer, whether quality can be higher and whether the experience can be better for everyone involved.
A culture of excellence is therefore closely connected to psychological ownership. When people feel that a project belongs to them as much as it belongs to the organisation, they tend to care more deeply about its outcome. They are more likely to take responsibility, anticipate problems and remain committed when difficulties arise.
Successful projects can also create positive momentum. One achievement can influence the atmosphere surrounding the next project.
Enthusiasm becomes contagious. Teams that have experienced the satisfaction of achieving something together often approach subsequent challenges with greater energy and optimism. In this way, success can become a catalyst for further success.
Importantly, organisations should recognise that not every project will be successful. Delays, mistakes and unexpected obstacles are inevitable in working life. What matters is how teams respond. A workplace that treats every setback as failure can discourage initiative. A workplace that treats setbacks as opportunities to learn can preserve motivation while encouraging resilience.
The most powerful teams therefore learn to celebrate both achievement and progress. They recognise the final result while appreciating the discipline, cooperation and perseverance that made it possible. This creates an environment where people understand that excellence is not about perfection. It is about consistently striving to improve.
Ultimately, successfully completing a workplace project can ignite motivation because it provides your team with a powerful combination of achievement, recognition and confidence. It demonstrates that collective effort produces meaningful results. More importantly, it can inspire people to raise their own expectations and those of the team around them.
When success is followed by reflection, recognition and a commitment to continuous improvement, each completed project becomes more than an isolated accomplishment. It becomes a building block for professional growth and organisational excellence. Teams begin to understand that today's achievement is not the destination but the foundation upon which tomorrow's higher standard can be built.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lima: Alternative venues being explored amid rising regional competition — Khaled
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: The proposal to explore an alternative venue for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima) in the future is aimed at keeping the event competitive amid growing competition among defence exhibitions in the region.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said continuous improvements to Lima, particularly in terms of venue size and facilities, were necessary, especially as more neighbouring countries were also organising similar exhibitions.
"The competition to organise such exhibitions is very, very strong.
"If we do not improve the facilities and expand the area, we may see fewer participants.
"Indonesia and Vietnam do it, Thailand does it as well. That's why we have to constantly make improvements," he told reporters after presenting the National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) Loan Advance payment (WPP) to 172 recipients here today.
He said this when asked to comment on former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad's view that Lima should remain in Langkawi, as the event had already established itself as an internationally recognised brand.
Tun Dr Mahathir was reported to have said that if the existing facilities in Langkawi could no longer accommodate the exhibition's growing requirements, the government should explore other options to ensure international industry participation was not affected.
His remarks follow Mohamed Khaled's earlier statement that the government would explore the possibility of holding Lima in Melaka in the future.
Mohamed Khaled said the government should consider developments in the defence exhibition industry in neighbouring countries, which now offer more extensive facilities and exhibition space.
"If, for example, Langkawi is too small to accommodate the exhibition, then we have to look for (an alternative). Otherwise, we may see fewer participants than expected.
"That's why I mentioned an area that can accommodate more people and make it easier for them to come," he said.
Mohamed Khaled said Klebang in Melaka was among the locations that could be considered, but major investment would be needed to develop suitable convention and exhibition facilities.
He also cited the organisation of Defence Services Asia (DSA) at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec) in the federal capital, saying the venue faced space constraints, particularly for displaying large defence assets and vehicles.
He said international defence exhibitions in countries such as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates were held in venues with large exhibition areas on a single level, in addition to open spaces for displaying various defence assets.
"In Kuala Lumpur, we had to put all the vehicles inside and there was not enough space to accommodate them.
"So, perhaps (we can consider other locations), but the parties involved need to invest in providing the necessary facilities. If we do not do this, many people may not participate in the exhibition we are organising," he said.
Asked whether the Lima name would be retained if the exhibition were moved to another location, Mohamed Khaled said it was still too early to decide. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal Floods: Prioritise mental health support for families of missing Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wisma Putra has been called on to act swiftly and prioritise mental health support for families of Malaysians still missing following the Nepal disaster.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih) member Dr R. Manivannan said families should not have to wait days for psychological support while facing prolonged uncertainty over their loved ones.
He cited a family member in Perak who sought help from the ministry's psychologist on Sept 2, but was referred to the Social Welfare Department and given a counselling appointment only for Sept 9 due to the counsellor's existing appointments.
"We simply do not see the urgency in this response.
"Acute psychological distress can develop within hours or days following an extremely traumatic event," he said in a statement today.
Manivannan said such delays could discourage other affected families from seeking help.
"How can we expect other family members to reach out for support if they know that it may take seven days or more before help is provided?
"Families who are already struggling may feel discouraged from seeking assistance if they believe they will be left waiting for a week," he said.
He said the collection of DNA samples had also added to the distress faced by some families.
"We are dealing with immediate trauma in an extraordinary situation," he said.
Manivannan urged Wisma Putra to establish a dedicated team of psychologists and counsellors to provide rapid support, including home visits and urgent assessments.
He said the ministry should reach out directly to next-of-kin rather than wait for them to seek help, as some may be in denial or reluctant to ask for assistance.
"Families should not be expected to take the first step when they are experiencing shock, denial, grief and prolonged uncertainty.
Manivannan said affected families were mainly in the Klang Valley, Perak and Penang, and offered to mobilise qualified psychologists and counsellors if Wisma Putra could assist with transport and logistics.
"We are asking for the available resources to be mobilised now, while the families are in need, rather than after a crisis develops," he said.
On Sept 3, Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the ministry was ready to
provide psychosocial support to affected families
and was awaiting updates from the Foreign Ministry to coordinate assistance.
Meanwhile today, Malaysia has also deployed an 11-member Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) to Nepal for a seven- to 10-day humanitarian mission, with
locating Malaysians
who remain uncontactable among its immediate priorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Masseuse dies after falling from fourth-floor shoplot while fleeing inspection
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 36-year-old foreign masseuse died after falling from the fourth floor of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Permas Jaya, Masai, while allegedly trying to flee an enforcement inspection two days ago.
Johor Baru Selatan deputy police chief Superintendent Ng Swie Chait said police received a report on the incident at 3.48pm.
"Initial investigations found that the woman allegedly fell from the fourth floor while trying to escape during an inspection by the Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) at the premises where she worked.
"The victim was found lying face down behind the shoplot with bleeding to the head," he said in a statement today.
Ng said the body was sent to the forensic department at Sultan Ismail Hospital here for a post-mortem.
"The post-mortem found that the cause of death was a fractured skull and several broken ribs.
"Police are still completing investigations from various angles, and the classification of the case may be changed if the post-mortem report or new evidence indicates otherwise," he said.
He said the case was currently classified as sudden death, and urged the public not to speculate about the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas-Umno cooperation should continue until GE16, says Mubarak chief
Article:
KOTA BARU: The growing cooperation between Pas and Umno is a positive development that should be sustained at least until the 16th General Election (GE16).
Kelantan Council of Former Elected Representatives (Mubarak) president Datuk Mohd Rozali Isohak said such cooperation should have taken place long ago.
"This kind of cooperation could strengthen Malay and Muslim unity after years of waiting for the two major Malay-based parties to work together.
"In my opinion, this cooperation is something that should be continued, at least until GE16.
"It is a very encouraging development for the unity of the Malays and Muslims.
"The time is right for this cooperation after we have waited for so long," said the 76-year-old who was former Kelantan deputy Menteri Besar.
Rozali said there were historical precedents for Pas and Umno working together, including their cooperation under Barisan Nasional following the May 13, 1969 incident, as well as the Angkatan Perpaduan Ummah (APU) coalition in the 1990 general election.
However, he noted that the APU experience was different as Pas was working with Semangat 46, a splinter party formed by former Umno members.
"I was involved in managing the APU cooperation at that time. There were many challenges that had to be resolved.
"I was the chief negotiator representing Semangat 46, while the late Tan Sri Nik Abdul Aziz Nik Mat represented Pas," he said.
Rozali said the experience had taught political leaders that any cooperation between parties required patience, understanding and the ability to resolve differences.
He said the current cooperation between Pas and Umno should therefore be viewed positively, while lessons from previous political collaborations should be taken into account.
He added that the most important consideration was ensuring that the cooperation could contribute towards political stability and strengthen unity among Malays and Muslims.
"After all, we have gone through various experiences. We should learn from the past and ensure that this cooperation is managed properly for the benefit of the people," he said.
Pas and Umno have been moving towards renewed political cooperation ahead of GE16.
The latest rapprochement has included discussions between leaders of both parties on possible cooperation and seat arrangements, although Umno has stressed that no formal pact or revival of Muafakat Nasional has been agreed.
The cooperation gained further momentum in recent months, with Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang saying in July that working with Umno was necessary to strengthen Malay-Muslim political unity.
The issue has also featured prominently during Pas' current muktamar in Kota Baru, with senior Umno leaders attending PAS events.
Pas has also indicated that it is prepared for GE16, including the possibility of an early election.
However, the nature and extent of the cooperation remain fluid.
Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi previously ruled out reviving Muafakat Nasional, suggesting that any future cooperation could take a different form.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sydney sweats in spring hot spell, faces 'extreme' bushfire risk
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia's most populous city Sydney baked in a burst of sweltering spring heat on Saturday, raising the risk of bushfires and prompting authorities to issue a ban on lighting fires.
The heat comes as a powerful El Nino weather pattern in the Pacific, expected to be among the strongest in decades, drives hotter and drier conditions across southern Australia during the September-November spring season.
On Saturday, the nation's weather forecaster said temperatures in the New South Wales capital, home to 5.6 million people, were set to hit 33°C (91.4°F), nearly 13°C above average.
At Sydney Airport, the temperature was already 28.6°C (83.48°F) at 11.30am (0130 GMT) local time, more than seven degrees above the September mean maximum temperature, according to forecaster data.
"Fresh to strong and gusty northwesterly winds developing during the morning, combined with dry, unseasonably warm conditions, will result in elevated fire dangers across the Greater Sydney Region today," the forecaster said.
State fire authorities issued a total fire ban for Sydney, where they rated fire risk as "extreme", the second-highest danger rating.
Climate change is causing extreme heat and fire weather to become more common in Australia, a bushfire-prone country of around 27 million.
In January, thousands of firefighters battled bushfires in the southeast that razed homes, cut power to thousands of homes and burned swathes of bushland.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas hopes no 'fire-starters' will derail unity of ummah
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas is hoping there will be no more "fire-starters" burning bridges or "invisible hands" working to derail its agenda of ummah (Muslim community) unity.
Pas Indera Mahkota delegate Nasrudin Hassan Tantawi said unity did not mean sacrificing principles, but rather strengthening the Muslim community, managing differences with decorum and prioritising the interests of Islam.
"Ummah unity is not merely a political strategy. To make this agenda a success, we must change a political culture that punishes into one that educates.
"We have proposed this unity agenda many times, but on several occasions, we have faced failure.
"I hope this time there will be no more fire-starters burning the bridges that have already been built and no more invisible hands performing sleight of hand to derail this agenda."
He said this while supporting a motion to strengthen the ummah unity agenda towards consolidating Malay-Muslim political strength and national stability.
At the same time, he reminded party members, leaders and supporters to use social media as a platform for unity rather than division.
"Members, leaders and supporters must be nurtured so that differences, however small, among us are not turned into ammunition or weapons to undermine unity.
"Let us not lose 1,000 hearts that are drawing closer to the Islamic cause we champion simply because we want to win an argument with netizens on social media," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anak Krakatau continues to erupt, lava fountains reported
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, continued to erupt on Saturday morning, with booming and rumbling sounds heard from an observation post as authorities reported lava-fountaining activity.
National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Disaster Data, Information and Communication Centre Acting Head Berton Panjaitan said the eruption began at 11.07pm local time on Friday and continued throughout the observation period from midnight to 6am on Saturday.
He said the Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (PVMBG) had assessed that the volcano's regrown edifice remained relatively small and was not considered capable of collapsing on a scale that could trigger a tsunami, amid concerns among residents along coastal areas.
"The government is addressing concerns among the public, particularly along the coasts of Banten and Lampung over a potential tsunami linked to Anak Krakatau given their experience of the Dec 22, 2018 tsunami," he said in a statement on Saturday.
Anak Krakatau, administratively located in South Lampung regency, Lampung province, remains at Level III, or Siaga (Alert), with authorities maintaining a three-kilometre exclusion zone around its active crater.
Between midnight and 6am on Saturday, PVMBG recorded one eruption earthquake with an amplitude of 70 millimetres and a duration of 21,600 seconds, while a field surveillance camera was knocked out after being struck by ejected volcanic material.
"The public is asked not to approach the volcanic area to observe the eruption or take photographs or videos, considering that there is still the potential for material to be ejected from the active crater," he said.
Meanwhile, about 650 people from 208 families have been registered as evacuees following increased activity at Mount Sinabung in Karo regency, North Sumatra, after its Aug 31 eruption prompted authorities to raise the volcano's status from Level II (Waspada) to Level III (Siaga).
Berton said about 405 people remained at the Jambur Arih Ersada evacuation centre in Sukatepu village as of Friday, while the extent of damage to agricultural land from volcanic ash was still being assessed.
He noted that thick white crater smoke was observed rising about 300 to 500 metres above Sinabung's summit between noon and 6pm on Friday, although no seismic activity was recorded during the period.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas at 75: Quiet celebration, louder political message
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas marked its 75th anniversary at Pusat Tarbiyah Islamiyah Kelantan in Pengkalan Chepa here last night without the grandeur of a milestone celebration.
Instead, the diamond jubilee was observed simply, reflecting the character the party has sought to project throughout its political journey — grassroots support, modesty and religious identity.
The gathering drew some 30,000 Pas delegates and observers attending the party's 72nd Muktamar, along with members and their families.
The focus was on those who have sustained the party through decades of political turbulence rather than the spectacle of the occasion.
That simplicity takes on added meaning as Pas enters a potentially consequential period in its political history.
After seven and a half decades, Pas is no longer merely an opposition force. Its growing electoral influence and central role in Perikatan Nasional (PN) have put it at the centre of national political calculations, particularly ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
Yet its leadership insists electoral success cannot come at the expense of its principles.
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the party would not sacrifice its principles simply to win power or reach Putrajaya.
That message comes as Pas faces a bigger challenge – turning its longstanding ideological identity into a broader political proposition capable of reaching beyond its traditional support base.
Its recent engagement with Umno adds another layer to the equation.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party would support any agenda that could strengthen Malay unity and political stability, signalling a willingness to engage on issues that could bring the two Malay-majority parties closer despite their different political positions.
For Pas, however, cooperation cannot be reduced to electoral arithmetic.
The party has repeatedly maintained that political cooperation must remain consistent with its principles and direction.
The balancing act is clear – expand its political reach without convincing its core supporters that growth will dilute its identity.
Against that backdrop, the understated anniversary celebration at the convention centre offered a striking contrast.
The occasion was modest. The political questions confronting Pas are anything but.
After 75 years, the party appears to be entering a new phase – one in which the challenge is no longer simply survival, but turning its longevity, grassroots machinery and growing influence into a credible national alternative.
The simplicity of the celebration may reflect a party that still sees itself as a movement first and a political machine second.
But as Pas looks towards GE16 and potentially Putrajaya, its next chapter will be measured not by how it celebrates 75 years, but by how it balances principles, political cooperation, Malay unity and the pursuit of federal power.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hot-air balloon basket kills German tourist in Switzerland
Article:
GENEVA: An 86-year-old German man died after being struck by the basket of a hot-air balloon on a meadow in Switzerland near Lake Constance, canton Thurgau police said on Friday, reported German news agency dpa.
The man, from the Konstanz district, succumbed to his serious injuries at the scene.
He had been part of a group, some of whom intended to take part in the balloon flight, a police spokesman told dpa. The accident occurred on Thursday evening during the launch process.
How it happened is still under investigation.
The balloon was due to take off from a meadow near Salen-Reutenen, around 20 kilometres west of the city of Konstanz.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PIL2A first phase reaches 29.85pct completion, paving way to Silicon Island
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The first phase of the Pan Island Link 2A (PIL2A) has reached 29.85 per cent completion, with work progressing 0.42 per cent ahead of schedule.
The RM420 million first phase involves a 1.5km road and marine bridge linking an interchange at Jalan Permatang Damar Laut directly to Silicon Island.
State Infrastructure and Transport Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the progress reflected the commitment of the Penang government, project developer and contractors to ensuring smooth project implementation.
"The state government will continue to closely monitor the implementation of this project through close cooperation with Penang Infrastructure Corporation Sdn Bhd, the project developer and contractors to ensure the project progresses smoothly and challenges at the site can be addressed effectively," he said today.
The marine bridge uses a Balanced Cantilever Beam structure, with construction of sub-structures such as pile caps and piers currently underway in marine and land areas at Permatang Damar Laut.
The project requires 260 T-beams for its superstructure, with 25 units having completed casting as of Aug 31.
Zairil said the first section of the marine bridge is expected to be completed and opened to the public in December 2028, followed by full completion of PIL2A in June 2029.
The 5.3km PIL2A is a key component of the Penang Transport Master Plan (PTMP) and is planned as the main link between Penang Island and the future Silicon Island development in Bayan Lepas.
The highway will connect Silicon Island with the Sultan Abdul Halim Muadzam Shah Bridge, also known as the Second Penang Bridge.
In April last year, the Chief Minister's Office said
land acquisition
in the southern part of the island for PIL2A Phase 1 at Permatang Damar Laut had been carried out in accordance with legal provisions.
At the time, construction was tentatively scheduled to begin in 2025, with land acquisition expected to commence in June that year.
The latest progress comes as the project continues to advance towards providing a permanent route to Silicon Island through Jalan Permatang Damar Laut.
Zairil said given that the alignment passes through residential areas, they are maintaining communication with affected communities, particularly in relation to temporary road diversions and closures.
"Safety standards, operational controls and environmental management also remain priorities throughout construction, with project management continuing to monitor works at the site," he added.
"Once completed, PIL2A Phase 1 is expected to strengthen connectivity to Silicon Island while supporting future development and sustainable urban growth in Penang," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal floods: 55 Malaysians still uncontactable after 10 days
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Ten days after devastating floods struck the Nepal-China border region, the fate of 55 Malaysians who remain unreachable is still unknown, according to Wisma Putra.
"The ministry remains in direct contact with their next of kin and continues to provide updates as search, verification and related efforts continue," it said in a statement.
It said information on individual cases was being communicated directly to families, while public updates would be limited to verified information.
Wisma Putra is also seeking confirmation from China through diplomatic channels over possible overlaps between reports of Malaysians in Nepal and those reported to be in Tibet.
"The Malaysian Embassy in Beijing remains in contact with Chinese authorities, while the ministry is also engaging the Chinese Embassy in Kuala Lumpur for official clarification," it said.
Malaysia has also expressed its readiness to provide appropriate search-and-rescue expertise if requested by Chinese authorities.
It said Malaysia's response was being coordinated through its headquarters in Putrajaya, the Malaysian embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing, and the Malaysian High Commission in New Delhi.
Efforts to locate the Malaysians and verify their status are supported by the National Security Council (NSC), National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), police, Chemistry Department and other relevant agencies.
Today, Malaysia deployed an 11-member Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) to Nepal as part of its humanitarian response to the disaster.
The
team departed
Subang Air Base aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force A400M aircraft, carrying equipment including communications gear.
On Aug 26, severe floods and landslides struck Rasuwa district near the Nepal-China border, sweeping through areas along the Trishuli River valley.
Believed to have been triggered by a glacier collapse, the disaster also hit Rasuwagadhi, a key crossing between Nepal and Tibet used by tourists and pilgrims travelling to Mount Kailash.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PSM urges halt to PPR Taman Manggis evictions as housing board defends enforcement
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) has urged Penang authorities to halt evictions at PPR Taman Manggis, while the Penang Housing Board defended the action.
PSM Penang said five units at the People's Housing Programme (PPR) Taman Manggis were locked by authorities on Sept 3, with several more residents allegedly facing eviction.
PSM Penang spokesman Choo Chon Kai said residents deemed to have lost their eligibility were being evicted without being offered permanent housing alternatives.
He claimed some grounds for disqualification were unreasonable, including a resident allegedly losing eligibility after marrying a foreigner despite having been married for years and heirs of original tenants who had died and were required to vacate their units.
"Affected residents had submitted appeals to the board but some have yet to receive responses before units were locked.
"Such eviction action is inhumane. The board and the Penang government should consider the appeals carefully," it said.
Choo also called for affordable permanent housing options, including Rent-To-Own (RTO) schemes, to be offered to those who no longer qualified for PPR but still required housing.
He further urged the state government to review eligibility requirements for PPR and Penang government rental housing, saying existing income thresholds were outdated.
The previous thresholds of RM750 for an individual applicant and RM1,500 for household income did not reflect current economic realities, particularly with the minimum wage now at RM1,700, he added.
The Housing and Local Government Ministry allows households with gross monthly income of up to RM3,000 to apply for PPR, while Perak has raised its household income threshold to RM3,860.
Meanwhile, the Penang Housing Board said
enforcement
against the affected units was not carried out abruptly but followed cross-checks, detailed assessments, engagement sessions and the issuance of notices in accordance with government procedures.
It said the PPR scheme was intended as transitional or temporary housing for low-income B40 families, allowing them to rent at heavily subsidised rates while stabilising their household finances.
The board said rent at PPR Taman Manggis remained RM124 a month despite increases in the minimum wage.
"Tenancy agreements are for three years and renewal is not automatic, with tenants required to undergo reassessment upon expiry," it stressed.
The board said investigations found breaches involving several units, including tenants who owned other property, households whose income exceeded the eligibility limit, units being sublet to third parties and violations of house rules.
"Enforcement is necessary to ensure fairness to other applicants who remain on the waiting list," it said.
On claims that residents were not offered permanent alternatives, the board said it had conducted outreach sessions and interviews with affected tenants and heirs as early as Jan 16, last year.
It said eligible residents were advised to consider the RTO scheme if they no longer qualified to remain under PPR, describing it as a potential long-term and permanent housing solution.
"Affected residents had been given sufficient time to make relocation arrangements.
"Notices of termination and vacant possession were issued on Dec 31, last year, with an adjustment period until March 31, this year.
"However, physical enforcement was only carried out on Sept 3, giving affected families additional time to seek alternative accommodation," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Smart's main focus in Nepal is locating missing Malaysians
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) is expected to remain in Nepal for seven to 10 days to assist in the humanitarian mission following devastating floods.
National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the 11 officers and personnel deployed had various specialised skills, including search and rescue (SAR), drone operations, logistics, communications and technical support.
"The flight departed at 9am and will take about five hours. They are expected to arrive at 11am Nepal time (1pm Malaysian time).
"We are bringing 12.4 tonnes of equipment, including rescue gear, detection devices, communication systems, high-capacity drones, specialised tunnel rescue equipment, a four-wheel-drive vehicle and a 10-tonne truck," he said at a press conference at the Subang Air Base here today.
Meor Ismail said the team's area of deployment would only be known upon arrival, after which Malaysian representatives in Nepal would brief them on the operational area.
Earlier, it was reported that the 11 Smart officers and personnel departed for Nepal aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force A400M aircraft to assist in the humanitarian mission in disaster-hit areas.
On the team's objectives, Meor Ismail said its priority was to provide humanitarian assistance, including SAR operations, with the immediate focus on locating Malaysians who remained uncontactable.
He said Smart was expected to be deployed to the last known location of the missing Malaysians based on information gathered.
"Usually, after being briefed by our counterparts in Nepal, they will be provided with a guide for operations there.
"Our target is to assist the humanitarian mission. In SAR, we do not differentiate between victims. Whoever we find, we will rescue them. We do not know where our people who have lost contact are.
"However, our focus is on the last known location of the Malaysians. That is our main priority. We certainly want to find our people, so their last known location will be our focus," he said.
Yesterday, it was reported that the whereabouts of 55 Malaysians who could not be contacted following devastating flash floods in Nepal on Aug 26 remained unknown.
Wisma Putra was reported to have said the figure was based on the latest information received from family members, travel agencies and other relevant sources.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chew Jetty unaffected by fire 20m away, says Penang CM
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Chew Jetty waterfront community was not affected by or involved in this morning's fire, which broke out about 20 metres away.
"Chew Jetty is not affected and is not involved in this fire. The fire site is about 20 metres from Chew Jetty," Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said when visiting the site this morning.
Chow said the fire, reported about 1am, involved six premises comprising workshops, a carpentry business and other businesses.
He said the blaze was brought under control by the Fire and Rescue Department, with assistance from volunteer firefighters.
"Firefighters are still carrying out work to complete the operation, including removing timber and other materials from the site.
"The timber comprises construction materials, so a contractor has been arranged to remove them to allow the Fire and Rescue Department to complete its operation," he added.
Chow said the land belonged to the state government, while the premises were believed to have been occupied by tenants or holders of Temporary Occupation Licences (TOL).
He said the affected owners might be interested in rebuilding the premises and the state government would assist in the process.
"There were no fatalities or injuries. Thankfully," he said.
It was
reported
that swift action by the Penang Fire and Rescue Department prevented a fire involving five premises at Chew Jetty here early today from spreading to a nearby petrol station and residential units.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: "I stayed silent out of fear": Student recounts obscene conversation with e-hailing driver
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 19-year-old college student was traumatised after an e-hailing driver allegedly engaged in an obscene conversation during her ride from the Terminal Bersepadu Selatan to her hostel in Setapak.
The student, who wished to be identified as Putery, recorded part of the conversation, which later went viral on social media.
Putery, from Seremban, Negri Sembilan, said she took a bus to Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday and was supposed to arrive at the terminal at 9pm.
However, the bus was delayed and arrived about 1.30am.
"I had booked an e-hailing service while I was still in Seremban. Initially, I was assigned another driver, but the booking was cancelled after my bus was delayed.
"I was then assigned another driver. He contacted me and said he was near the terminal.
"I told him I was still on the way as my bus had been delayed. He asked me to contact him once I arrived," she said when contacted.
Putery contacted the driver after arriving at the terminal.
"On the way to the hostel, he asked about the delay before the conversation shifted to his personal experiences.
"He then asked whether I had any plans during the holidays.
"I told him I did not, as all my friends were holidaying in Thailand and I was only returning home to be with my family," she said.
Putery said the driver then began talking about Thailand, prostitution and his personal experiences.
"I only gave brief responses such as 'oh', 'really' and 'I understand' because I was uncomfortable, but he continued.
"He even used my body as an example while discussing sexual matters," she said.
Putery said the driver continued talking about sex throughout the journey.
"When we arrived at the hostel, he was still talking about it. He also showed me a type of pill which he claimed to have taken before having sex.
"The journey should have taken about 20 minutes, but it took longer even though the roads were clear in the early hours of the morning.
"I did not want to confront him because I am a woman and it was just the two of us. I was worried that if something happened, I might not be able to do anything.
"That was why I chose to remain silent until we reached my destination," she said.
Putery lodged a report at the Setapak police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC detains company owner for allegedly soliciting RM30,000 to secure defence‑sector financing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Kuala Lumpur has arrested an owner of a consulting, management and business company on suspicion of soliciting and accepting bribes of about RM30,000 in return for obtaining grants and loans under the Bumiputera entrepreneur financial financing scheme for two companies related to armaments and defence.
According to sources, the woman, in her 60s, was arrested at about 6.45pm on Thursday around Kuala Lumpur.
“Initial investigations found that the suspect committed the act in March 2025 and is suspected of soliciting and accepting bribes amounting to about RM30,000 from an owner of a company related to armaments and defence,” he said.
According to sources, a seven-day remand order until Sept 10 against the woman was issued by Magistrate Aliaa Anwar after an application was made by the MACC at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court yesterday morning.
Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib when contacted confirmed the arrest and the case is being investigated under Section 16(a) (A) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Serian tops very unhealthy API readings as six Sarawak areas exceed 200
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — A total of six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at very unhealthy levels as of 1pm today with Serian recording the highest reading of 287.
Deputy Director-General (Development) of the Department of Environment (DOE) Azuri Azizah Saedon said five other areas in the state that recorded very unhealthy readings were Kuching (267), Sri Aman (251), Samarahan (242), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201).
She said 25 areas recorded API readings at unhealthy levels involving Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Sabah, Labuan, Sarawak and Selangor, in addition to 26 areas recording moderate air quality status and 11 areas at good levels.
Azuri Azizah said the situation occurred amid persistent dry weather conditions in parts of the Southern Asean Region.
She said based on the report from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) yesterday, 139 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, Sumatra (138) and Malaysia (16), of which nine were in Sarawak, Sabah (five) and Terengganu (two).
“ASMC also reported that moderate to thick haze was observed moving northeast from Kalimantan to several areas in Sarawak, Sabah and Brunei.
“Moderate to thick smoke plumes were also observed in North Kalimantan and East Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra, while moderate haze was observed in Singapore, the southern part of the Peninsula and eastern Java,” he said in a statement today.
In this regard, she said the DOE continued to enhance monitoring and patrols in risky areas including forests, peatlands, landfills, agricultural and plantation areas and industrial areas that could potentially be the source of open burning.
Azuri Azizah said any source of open burning or pollution identified would be investigated and enforcement action would be taken strictly in accordance with the provisions of the law and the jurisdiction of the DOE.
The public is requested to immediately report any fire or open burning incidents to the Fire and Rescue Department via 999 or the DOE toll-free line 1-800-88-2727 to enable immediate action to be taken.
The latest API reading can be consulted through DOE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) at apims.doe.gov.my website or the MyJAS application. — Bernama

Title: In Nepal for eight days, Malaysian wife presses on with search for missing special‑operations firefighter
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Hani Othman, who has been in Nepal for eight days to follow the developments in the search for her missing Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) officer husband, today joined a mission to distribute humanitarian aid to disaster victims in the country, while hoping to find any clues as to her husband.
Hani, who is currently on her way from Nuwakot to Betrawati with the local non-governmental organisations (NGO) Samundra Nepal NGO and Himalayan Leaders, said that the area they are heading to is not the last location where her husband’s vehicle was detected, but she still hopes that the journey will yield clues.
“The area of my husband’s last point is further up. It’s difficult to access. But Nuwakot is also a disaster-prone area, just located further down.
“I will distribute aid to the victims here. Let’s see, who knows, we might find some clues,” she said when contacted by Bernama.
Hani said that some of the aid items were collected earlier in Kathmandu, while the rest were donated by local NGOs.
Meanwhile, through a social media post, Hani shared that yesterday she managed to distribute aid to disaster victims around Kathmandu, including those who were recently rescued in Timure, and also met the wife of her husband’s team vehicle driver.
She said the contributions from Malaysians were channelled on behalf of her husband, Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, and eight other members of his expedition team, including Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) deputy director of the Fire and Rescue Operations Division Mohd Sani Harul.
“As long as I have known them, they are all good people. They are also generous and like to help others. May Allah ease all their search endeavours and protect them all no matter where they are.
“Set aside religious and ethnic differences for now, let’s pray for the best for all of them,” she said.
So far, Hani has not received news of any new developments regarding the fate of her husband who was reported missing in the flood tragedy in Rasuwa, Nepal on August 26.
Two days after the incident, Hani flew to Kathmandu on her own initiative to get the latest updates on the search and rescue efforts for her husband.
Mohd Fakhrul, 44, was reported missing after the four-wheel drive vehicle his group was in during an expedition to Everest Base Camp (EBC) was believed to have been affected by floods while in a valley in Rasuwa.
A total of 55 Malaysians have been reported as still unreachable following the disaster that occurred on August 26, while 77 others who were found safe in Tibet and Nepal have been brought to Kathmandu to undergo processing before returning to Malaysia.
Anadolu Agency reported that the death toll from the disaster has risen to 1,220, while 4,762 people, including 844 foreigners, are still missing. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia sends families’ DNA samples to Nepal to help identify 55 missing Malaysians, says Tok Mat
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 5 — All DNA samples from the next-of-kin of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal have been obtained, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said the samples would be sent to Nepal for the authorities there to conduct DNA matching, a process expected to take some time given the large number of victims involved.
Mohamad said Malaysia was also prepared to send experts from the Department of Chemistry to assist the Nepalese authorities with the DNA matching process, if required.
“Many other countries will also be sending their experts to assist Nepal in identifying DNA matches for the victims, which will help expedite the process,” he told reporters after attending the Pinggiran Senawang Independence Carnival here today.
Meanwhile, he said the Nepalese government had been providing excellent cooperation to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu in obtaining the latest information on Malaysians affected by the disaster.
Mohamad said the ministry received daily updates from the Chargé d’Affaires of the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu on the search operation and the situation on the ground, while the next-of-kin were also contacted regularly whenever there were new developments.
He said Nepal had limited the entry of foreign search and rescue (SAR) teams to avoid having too many teams on the ground, which could make it more difficult for the local authorities to coordinate the operation.
This morning, 11 officers and personnel from Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) departed for Nepal to assist in SAR operations in areas affected by floods and landslides. The mission is expected to last 10 days.
A total of 55 Malaysians were reported still uncontactable following the disaster on Aug 26, while some of the 77 individuals located safe in Tibet and Nepal have since returned safely to Malaysia. The remainder are expected to return on flights arranged by their respective travel agents.
In another development, Mohamad said he would meet Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow in the capital on Monday to discuss efforts to enhance security in southern Thailand, as well as bilateral issues between the two countries.
He said Malaysia had been given the honour by Thailand to serve as a facilitator in negotiations with the parties concerned to help bring about peace in the region.
He added that the meeting would also discuss the best approach to ensure that efforts to promote security and peace in southern Thailand could be effectively implemented.
Mohamad said peace in the region would benefit both countries, particularly by boosting Malaysia-Thailand border trade, which is of significant value.
He also advised Malaysians planning to visit Thailand to remain vigilant and always prioritise their safety. — Bernama

Title: Chew Jetty heritage site unaffected by blaze, Penang govt to help owners of five destroyed premises, says CM
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The historic Chew Jetty here was unaffected by a fire that broke out about 20 metres away and destroyed five business premises early this morning, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the state government was ready to provide assistance to the owners of the five business premises, including support for rebuilding efforts.
“This involves government land. I believe the owners of the affected premises are either tenants or Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) holders.
“Should the owners decide to rebuild the affected premises, the state government will assist in the process,” he told reporters after visiting the fire site today, accompanied by Tanjung MP Lim Hui Ying, who is also Deputy Minister of Women, Family and Community Development.
Five business premises near the Chew Jetty area here, including a car workshop, a welding shop and a timber factory, were destroyed in a fire that broke out at 1.08am today, with no casualties reported.
Chow said the Penang Fire and Rescue Department, assisted by the Volunteer Fire Brigade, had brought the fire under control, while efforts to remove the timber stacks continued after traces of the fire were detected in the wooden structures.
Situated along George Town’s iconic waterfront, Chew Jetty is part of the Unesco World Heritage Site and has been home to generations of the Chinese community since the 19th century. — Bernama

Title: ‘If Langkawi too small’: Defence minister says LIMA may need alternative venue
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 5 — The proposal to explore an alternative venue for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) in the future is aimed at keeping the event competitive amid growing competition among defence exhibitions in the region.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said continuous improvements to LIMA, particularly in terms of venue size and facilities, were necessary, especially as more neighbouring countries were also organising similar exhibitions.
